title: EventEmitter basics
idea: An EventEmitter lets one part of your program announce that something happened, while any number of listeners react to it.

analogy.text: A radio station broadcasts a song and every tuned-in radio plays it. The station never knows who is listening.
analogy.breaks: Listeners run one after another, in the order they signed up.

points: `on(name, fn)` registers a listener; `once` runs it only one time.
`emit(name, ...args)` calls every listener, synchronously, in order.
Emitting an `error` event with no listener throws and can crash Node.

edges.label: publishes
edges.caption: Your code calls emit('order', 7). The emitter looks up everyone registered for 'order'.

edges.label: 1st
edges.caption: The first listener runs to completion. Nothing else runs yet.

edges.label: 2nd
edges.caption: Then the second listener runs. Same arguments, in registration order.

code.caption: Edit it: add a third listener, or change once to on, and run again.

pitfalls: `emit('error')` with no 'error' listener throws, so always handle it.
Listeners run synchronously: a slow listener blocks the emitter.
Forgotten `on` listeners pile up and leak memory; remove them with `off`.

quiz.q: What does the last line print?
quiz.why: `once` removed itself after the first emit, leaving the two `on` listeners.

takeaway: Emit announces, listeners react, and the emitter keeps the list.

starters: When would I use an EventEmitter in a real app?
What is the difference between on and once?
How do I stop a memory leak from listeners?
